data.narrative:
Physical Intelligence, a Series B AI & Software company founded by Hausman, Levine, Finn, and Ichter, is valued at $5.6B post-money following $600M+ in total capital raised. The valuation assessment draws from a peer set of 3 same-stage private companies and 1 public comparable (Palantir), with additional reference to frontier-AI firms including Scale AI, Black Forest Labs, Field AI, and Figure AI.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, anchored to the $5.6B last post-money valuation, applied a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier to arrive at $10.6B. The peer-median method examined three same-sector, same-stage private companies—Scale AI ($29.0B), Black Forest Labs ($3.2B), and Field AI ($2.0B)—yielding a median valuation of $3.2B. This peer set reflects substantial dispersion, with a range of $2.0B to $29.0B, indicating heterogeneous market pricing within the cohort.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $2.8B (low) to $12.2B (high), with a median of $6.9B. The current $5.6B valuation sits within this range, approaching the midpoint. Key uncertainties stem from the limited peer sample (n=3) and extreme outlier variance within that sample, where Scale AI's $29B valuation substantially exceeds the median. The stage-progression method's reliance on historical multipliers may not fully capture the idiosyncratic risk profile of frontier-technology businesses, warranting caution in extrapolating stage-based step-ups.
